the cardiovascular system is a part of the reward mechanism, but that the exact role of the cardiovascular system in the reward mechanism is not known.

the cardiovascular responses to intracranial brain stimulation are not only a reflection of a generalized autonomic activation, but that the cardiovascular changes are also an important component of the rewarding property of the brain stimulation.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the brain stimulation-induced lever-pressing behavior is regulated by a feedback mechanism which involves the autonomic nervous system and that the brain stimulation reward is dependent on the cardiovascular state.
electrical stimulation of the brain can produce a variety of cardiovascular effects which may be mediated through afferent pathways from the cardiovascular system to the brain.
intracranial self-stimulation is a complex phenomenon involving both central and peripheral mechanisms.

the cardiovascular state is an important determinant of the reward property of brain stimulation, and that the cardiovascular state and brain stimulation reward property may have a mutual regulatory relationship.
